'''Fell Critters''' are small, beetle-like [[Fell]] that can be found throughout the [[Shroud]] in all biomes of [[Embervale]].

Some critters in later biomes are able to fly, and use this to patrol the area they reside in.

Critters are almost always found in swarms with anywhere from a handful to a few dozen members.

They are not to be confused with the larger, bright-red variant the [[Exploding Fell Critter]].
In their normal state, variants differ in their defenses: Cutting (Neutral or Effective); Piercing (Neutral or Effective).

==Attacks==
Critters attack by lunging toward the player and attempting to bite. 
'''Flying Critters''' will fly toward a player and perform an aerial lunge. Flying critters become briefly dazed and drop to the ground after receiving damage.

The danger of '''Fell Critters''' lies with their numbers, as large swarms of rapidly attacking critters can quickly overwhelm a player. They are best fought in a team, with area-damaging attacks, or by fighting while moving to stay ahead of the swarm.

==Spawning==
'''Fell Critters''' can spawn almost anywhere in the Shroud, but they are most often found in areas of heavy activity in the Shroud; this includes [[Elixir Well|Elixir Wells]], around [[Shroud Root|Shroud Roots]], and in ruined villages or towns within the Shroud.

In [[mycelium (Material)|mycelium]]-covered areas of the Shroud, '''Critters''' have a chance to spontaneously pop up from the ground to attack the player.

'''Fell Critter Nests''' will continuously spawn critters unless destroyed (best done using a [[felling Axes|felling axe]] or fire damage).

'''Fell Critters''' are also often spawned as secondary enemies in boss fights; with the [[Fell Critter Queen]] and [[Fell Wispwyvern]] both summoning critters in their fights.

'''Fell Draconian Vultures''' are a Shroud-infected [[Fell]] variant of [[Draconian Vulture|Draconian Vultures]] that are encountered in [[Shroud|Enshrouded areas]] of the Kindlewastes and Albaneve Summits.

They are vicious and difficult enemies that should be treated with caution.

==Attacks==
'''Shroud Pellet''' - The vulture can attack the player from a distance by spitting a Shroud projectile at them. It explodes on impact for moderate Shroud damage and leaves behind a small area of dense Shroud.

'''Talon Swipe''' - Once close, the vulture will swipe at the player with its razor-sharp talons. This deals '''heavy''' cutting damage and can do bonus Backstab damage (e.g. if the player is attempting to flee).

==Strategies==
Ranged and magic attacks are important to help keep the vultures at a distance, as their melee attack deals extremely high damage. 

In melee, the vulture's melee attack can be parried, and it will fall to the ground stunned after a few successful parries.

If you do not wish to engage with a vulture, it is recommended to use the [[glider]] to flee quickly; they are very difficult to outrun on foot.

Bestiary.text:
The land of Embervale is teeming with dangers and mysteries, inhabited by a wide variety of corrupted and wild beings, each with its own dark history.

===The Fell===
Once people and animals of the land, the Fell are now twisted by the corrupting influence of the Shroud—a creeping, fungal fog that spreads across Embervale like a living disease. These creatures are deformed, their flesh consumed by fungal growths, their minds lost to madness. Some retain a faint echo of their former selves, making their tragic existence even more terrifying. The Shroud itself pulses through their veins, binding them to its malevolent will.

===Scavengers===
Driven mad by overuse of the Elixir, these once-human scavengers now roam the wastelands in a frenzied state. Their eyes glow with an unnatural light, and their skin is marred by chemical burns from the potent substances they ingest. Desperation fuels their violence, and they attack anything in sight, eager for more Elixir to satiate their growing addiction. Scavengers are unpredictable, aggressive, and dangerous—creatures of chaos.

===The Vukah===
The elusive Vukah, a sentient species of animal-like beings, have begun to dominate the untamed regions of Embervale. Standing upright with fur-covered bodies, they possess a strange mix of primal strength and cunning intelligence. Similar in appearance to a cross between an Ewok and a Wookie, the Vukah use primitive technology and guerrilla tactics to protect their lands. They may seem primitive, but their keen survival instincts and fierce territorial nature make them formidable opponents.

===The Hollow===
Cursed and eternal, the Hollow are the restless undead that wander the cursed plains and dark corners of Embervale. Their flesh rots away, but their spirits remain tethered to the mortal world by dark magic. Drained of emotion and purpose, these tragic figures seek out the living, drawn to their warmth and life force. Beware their hollow eyes, for they see no future—only eternal hunger.

===The Drak===
The hateful reptilian species descended from Vesztah, the Broodmother, have returned to the shores of Embervale and have begun reclaiming the Veilwater Basin after previously being driven away to a nearby archipelago.  They are divided into 4 tribes and hold deep cultural and territorial rivalries.  They are known for their strength, resilience, and a fierce desire for glory and dominance, believing only the strongest rise to Ark Morgo, their afterlife realm.  They believe humans have usurped their rightful place as favorites of the Ancients.

===Flora of Embervale===
The plant life of Embervale is as dangerous as its inhabitants, adapted to the dark magic and corruption that plagues the land.

===Fauna of Embervale===
The wildlife of Embervale is a mix of corrupted beasts and natural predators, many of which have adapted to the harsh environment

===Passive Creatures===
Not all animals in Embervale are deadly. Some, like the Goats and Hophare (large, long-eared rabbits), are peaceful creatures, content to graze and hop along the fields.
Even amidst the chaos, domesticated animals like dogs and cats can still be found, loyal companions to those lucky enough to have them.

'''Exploding Fell Critters''' are large, beetle-like [[Fell]] that can be found alongside their [[Fell Critter|smaller cousins]] in mid to late-game [[Shroud]] areas.

They patrol their territory with their fellow critters until they spot a threat; upon which they will promptly scurry toward the intruder and self-detonate.

==Combat==
'''Exploding Fell Critters''' fight by rushing toward the nearest player and exploding after a (very) brief delay. This explosion causes heavy damage and can easily lead to a player's death.

When an '''exploding critter''' is preparing to explode, a small red ring will appear on the ground around them.

==Tips==
'''Exploding critters''' can be quite tricky to manage while dealing with critter swarms. Here are some tips for doing so:
* Attack from afar with a [[Bows|bow]], [[staff]], or explosives; targeting the '''exploding critters''' first.
* The critters' explosion damages other enemies as well. You can use this to thin their numbers a bit.
* Do not try to bait the explosion unless you are confident in your timing- the window is extremely short.

==Spawning==
'''Exploding Fell Critters''' first appear in the [[Nomad Highlands]] Shroud and can spawn anywhere that normal '''Critters''' are found.

In [[mycelium (Material)|mycelium]]-covered areas of the Shroud, '''Critters''' have a chance to spontaneously pop up from the ground to attack the player. ('''Exploding Critters''' are particularly dangerous here, watch out!)

'''Fell Critter Nests''' will continuously spawn critters unless destroyed (best done using a [[felling Axes|felling axe]] or fire damage).

Both normal '''Fell Critters''' and '''Exploding Fell Critters''' are summoned frequently during the [[Fell Critter Queen]] fight.

= Changelog for Patch #5 v.0.7.4.1 =

==Highlights==
* Added fixes for a few different crashes reported by the community.
* [[Well | Wells]] now have water again when discovered. When [[Well | wells]] are freshly placed in the player base, they still need a few minutes to fill up.
* [[Well | Wells]] now show a UI element indicating that they are currently refilling.
* Fixed several [[NPC]] and animal path-finding issues, for example finding and using [[beds]] has been made more reliable and pathfinding issues when going up and down stairs have been improved.
* Added new bathroom furniture pieces to the [[Albaneve_Summits | Albaneve Summits]] furniture set.
* Added more visual variations to the Fell melee soldiers in earlier areas of [[Embervale]].
* Rain is now stopped by roofs more reliably.
* Drying off after spending time in the rain is now faster when the player is sheltered.
* Fixed a few issues with quests not unlocking their next steps correctly.
* Reduced the frequency of rainy weather, but when it rains, it will rain a little bit longer than before. Even for November, this was too much.
* Quests that required the retrieval of villager souls could previously be blocked by player bases at the quest location. Now the quest is automatically solved in such cases.
* The quest for [[taming]] [[Common Goat || goats]] can now also be completed by [[taming]] [[Frizzy Goat | Frizzy Goats]].
* Fixed an issue with recipes not showing the unlocked event even though they unlocked correctly.

==Changelog==
===Improvements to Villagers and Animals===
* Increased the range in which [[:Category:Wild_Life | animals]] look for a [[bed]] and [[food]].
* [[NPC|NPCs]] were taught to properly sit on [[chairs]] and [[toilets]], to minimize accidents.
* There is now a small randomization for when [[NPC|NPCs]] decide to go to [[beds|bed]]. Before, when fast traveling to the player base it could be observed that everyone was heading to [[beds|bed]] at exactly the same time. This should make bedtime feel a bit more natural. Likewise, when returning to the base, not every NPC will jump out of [[beds|bed]] immediately at the same time.
* [[Fences]] and walls now better contain animals.
* [[Farm animals]] are no longer attacked by [[bees]].
* [[Cats]] are no longer alarmed by nearby [[Rat|rats]] while being [[Taming|tamed]]. It’s a fine balance between believable cat behavior and good gameplay…
* [[Cats]] and [[dogs]] can no longer be hit by players with [[Lightning Channel]] attacks.
* Lowered the height of the [[yak feeder]] prop so that both parents and calves can get to their [[food]] easily.
* Improved the placement sound and VFX for [[:Category:Wild_Life | animals]] and pets.
* Lowered the unnatural high speed of resource production from [[:Category:Wild_Life | animals]]. At the same time increased the maximum stack sizes of produced resources. As a side effect, this should lower the maintenance requirements for [[:Category:Wild_Life | animals]].
* [[baits|Bait]] stack sizes are now larger. This should also help against accidentally punching wildlife while trying to throw the next bait during the [[taming]] process.
* [[:Category:Wild_Life | Animals]] now realize more reliably when [[beds]] are placed in their vicinity.
* The rate at which [[:Category:Wild_Life | animals]] can have babies has been unified for all [[:Category:Wild_Life | animals]]. In the future, we will rebalance this again and better explain the [[reproduction]] rate, especially in case they will vary between different [[:Category:Wild_Life | animals]].
* When the [[taming]] has been completed, the UI now shows the success in a more comprehensible way.
* Picking up bait while [[:Category:Wild_Life | animals]] are eating it now correctly interferes with the [[taming]] process.
* Like [[Category:Enemies|enemies]], [[:Category:Wild_Life | animals]] now have less keen senses when it is [[raining]]. This makes it easier to hunt or tame them under bad [[weather]] conditions.
* After being [[taming|tamed]], [[:Category:Wild_Life | animals]] now also roam around when the player hasn't picked them up and dropped them off at their base, yet.
* Fixed the Beastmaster player [[skill]]. Befriended beasts can now be ordered to follow the player again.
* The first mouse click after tabbing out and back into the game will no longer trigger an in-game action. Previously, trying to regain focus of the game window could too easily lead to accidental weapon attacks or building actions.
* Fixed an issue where the game failed to gather the information about available happy [[villagers]] when the player tried to level up the flame in a player base that is not the one where the [[villagers]] are living.
* Crafting [[assistants]] can now offer the full range of recipes even if the crafting tools are placed in a different base.
* Fixed an issue that [[villagers]] would suddenly wake up in the middle of the night only to get back to bed right afterward again. Just because it’s happening to us it shouldn’t also happen to them…
* [[Villagers]] without beds are sleeping on the floor now as they should.
* [[Villagers]] no longer have trouble going to bed when they approach from the foot of the [[beds|bed]].
* [[Villagers]] no longer physically block doors or narrow stairs.
* The tutorial about needing happy [[villagers]] to level up the [[Flame]] no longer shows up every time the [[Flame]] menu is opened.
* Fixed that [[villagers]] can have multiple [[beds]] assigned in some cases.
* Fixed some situations in which [[villagers]] or [[:Category:Wild_Life | animals]] would interact with props through walls. One example was that they teleported through a wall to sit on a [[chairs|chair]].

===Fixes for new biome content and gameplay===
* Reduced the sturdiness of [[Silver Ore | silver]] and [[obsidian ore]]. While the yield per node is the same, it now takes less time to gather it.
* The UI for coldness and protection against it has been reworked after player feedback. The [[coldness]] meter now shows the encroaching freezing of the player. While exposed to extreme [[coldness]], this meter can only ever go up. Underneath the coldmeter, the level of [[coldness protection]] is displayed and the currently remaining time before [[hypothermia]] sets in. * The time can change rapidly depending on [[food]], [[consumables]], [[equipment]], [[torches]], nearby campfires and other factors.
* Added more information about the [[frost protection]] from the [[Flame]] at level 8 to the [[Flame]] upgrade screen and to the quest journal.
* Fixed an issue with the display of the “[[Hypothermia]]” warning that prevented it from showing up at the center of the screen initially.
* Increased the time before [[Hypothermia]] sets in for players without any kind of [[cold protection]] from 10 seconds to 20 seconds.
* Fixed that ice-sliding VFX could appear at the character's feet, even when they weren't touching the ground.
* Sliding down slopes now prevents using [[:Category:Ranged_Weapons|ranged weapons]].
* Added the previously missing area of effect damage for the spell [[Ice Bolt II]].
* Improved visibility of snowflakes when using DLSS.
* Fixed additional issues with the dynamic ambience sounds detection system leading to playing incorrect sounds or missing sounds for individual biomes.
* Fixed an issue with the quest to unlock 2 of the new [[Musical_Instruments#Music_Sheets|songs]]. The [[Musical_Instruments#Music_Sheets|songs]] can now be correctly unlocked.
* Fixed several small level-design issues such as floating props.
* Added a few more [[Category:Enemies|enemies]] to some empty areas in the [[Albaneve Summits]].
* Fixed a collision issue with one of the tree models which would lead to chopped wood to float out of the tree instead of dropping normally.
* Switched the visuals of the two granite [[Blocks#Roof_Blocks|roof blocks]] so that both fit better to the name and icon of the items.
* Updated the visuals of the [[balefire braziers]].
* Destroying the props in the [[Cyclops]] caves now triggers the correct VFX and sounds.
* Fixed discoloration on some fur parts on player [[Armor|armors]].
* Increased the size of the [[big spider]]. It’s meant to be a chonk.
* Fixed several smaller glitches for the [[Cyclops enemies]].
* Increased the damage to the stun bar of [[Fell_Dragon_Youngling | the boss]] when hitting it by parrying its own projectiles.
* Fixed an issue that could cause a spell or arrow to affect [[Fell_Dragon_Youngling | the boss]] stun bar twice.
* Removed the loot from the defeated [[Fell_Draconian_Vulture|vultures]] during [[Fell_Dragon_Youngling | the boss]] fight.
* Improved several animations and behavior glitches for [[Fell_Dragon_Youngling | the boss]].
* Added a subtle self-glow to the [[windows]] that look like they are made of glass. It’s not perfect yet but better than being completely black during the day.
* Exchanged an incorrect perk on the [[Horn Daggers]]. They now have correctly increased cut damage when upgraded.
* Improved the illuminated [[pumpkins]] for a prettier glow.
* Fixed an issue where the [[milk]] dropped from certain [[Category:Enemies|enemies]] as loot was mistakenly cooked already. It’s not that kind of cozy game.
* Fixed [[comfort]] category setting for [[tapestries]] and the [[granite throne]].
* Improved the UI overlay when [[Fell_Dragon_Youngling | the boss]] is unlocked.

===Miscellaneous Fixes===
* Updated the burning status VFX on the player to be more noticeable.
* Fixed one of the [[Shroud_Root|Shroud roots]] which didn’t clear the [[Shroud]] in the vicinity after being destroyed.
* Updated some old terrain textures to better fit the overall level of detail.
* Improved the level of detail for some mycelium-covered props.
* Fixed incorrect movement in armor pieces during an evasion roll.
* Removed several small glitches in [[Category:Enemies|enemy]]- and [[:Category:Wild_Life | animal]] animations.
* Fixed incorrect visuals and timings of several [[Category:Enemies|enemy]] attack VFXs.
* Fixed several small audio issues on enemies including [[Fell_Dragon_Youngling | the boss]], [[cyclops]], [[crocodiles]] and [[scavengers]].
* Added keyboard support to the split-stack sub-menu.
* Fixed incorrect sorting of several props in the recipe overview menus.
* Fixed an issue that could lead to the game freezing when tabbing out of the game window.
* Fixed one reason for a performance dip directly after teleporting longer distances.
* Slightly increased performance of rendering clouds.
* Switched back to the previous display of time for durations in the UI. At the same time further unified the display of durations. Sorry for the feet and inches, US players.
* Made the building shape preview tint more visible in direct sunlight.
* Brightness doesn’t reset during changes to the graphical quality settings.
* Fixed the saving of the time of day when quitting the game.
* Creating and playing a new world with a character that has the quest progression mode set to “missed quests” no longer blocks the first door in the Cinder Vault start cave.
* Fixed that the background sound ambience no longer resets when going to [[bdes|bed]].
* Fixed an issue with the recipe selection button in the workstation menus.
* Fixed a visual glitch when starting to fly with a [[gliders|glider]].
* Exchanged a 1-handed melee bonus from two armor pieces for the mage class Spellbinder Glove and Wizard Chest.
* Drastically increased the health for practice targets and dummies.
* Player tombstones were tweaked to minimize the risk that they can’t be looted properly depending on doors or other large props nearby.
* Selected quests are now deselected in the quest journal when they have been completed.
* Added a security measurement to make sure that grapple hook anchors are correctly interactive when the new grappling hook combat skills are unlocked and many enemies have gathered around the player.
* Fixed an issue with scrolling with a controller in the equipment menu.
* Made sure the ammunition display in the HUD remains visible even when the combat target is near the screen border.
* Fixed an issue where animations could sometimes not be played correctly when using ranged weapons.
* Fixed a few instances where loot dropped in regions it was not supposed to drop.
* Fixed an issue with the fade-to-black when fast traveling while having the HUD disabled.
* Fixed several issues with item icons.
* Fixed several cases where clicking on a quest map marker wouldn’t open the corresponding journal entry correctly.
* Fixed an issue that could lead to footsteps sounds not playing correctly.
* Improved performance for player bases with many villagers and large roaming distance set.
* The amount of data exchanged between servers and clients has been reduced. This should help in situations, where low bandwidth caused multiplayer issues previously.


A lot of these fixes wouldn't have happened without your reports, so as always, thanks for helping us make the game better!

== Overview ==
Dune Armadillos are tough, large animals found in the [[Kindlewastes]] region.

== Behavior ==
{{Behavior|Neutral}}

Dune Armadillos defend themselves when hit and return to their wildlife behavior after a period without further hits.

== Known Locations ==

=== Kindlewastes ===

* Found circling ruins northeast of [https://enshrouded.wiki.gg/wiki/Map?marker=SunsimmerSouterrain Sunsimmer Souterrain] (sightings of up to 3).
* Found near the oasis southeast of the [https://enshrouded.wiki.gg/wiki/Map?marker=AncientSpire-Kindlewastes Kindlewastes Ancient Spire]  (sightings of up to 7)

== Domestication ==

=== Taming ===
Dune Armadillos can be tamed with [[Dune Armadillo Food Bait]]. They require three successful pet interactions (💛💛💛) to be tamed.

After being brought to your base they require shelter, a [[Big Farm Animal Pillow]] and a [[Dune Armadillo Feeder]] with [[Dune Armadillo Food]]. You can craft these at the [[Farmer]] NPC.

=== Breeding ===
If provided with a spare bed, a pair of Dune Armadillos have a chance to produce offspring ([[Baby Dune Armadillo|Baby Dune Armadillos]]).

See [[Animal Husbandry|Animals Husbandry]] for breeding instructions, a complete list of farm animals, and more.

=== Produce ===
Dune Armadillos produce [[Scales]] when sheltered and fed. They can hold up to five (5) and won’t produce more beyond this limit until it's collected.

They will also produce when unfed, but at a much slower rate. Production will happen regardless of player distance.{{ItemsTableHeader
|content=
{{ItemsLine|image=Scales.png|item=Scales|quantity=1|type=Consumable|source=Product}}
}}

Uncollected produce ([[Scales]]) can remain in its inventory when it dies. This is separate from newly generated corpse loot.

== Enemy Resistances ==

Each enemy may be vulnerable or resistant to each damage type.

This vulnerability or resistance is encoded as a hidden multiplier to damage taken, that is unique for each enemy and damage type.

Any multiplier greater than 1 will display as "Effective" damage; any multiplier less than 1 will display as "Resisted" damage. 

'''Note that the increase/decrease in damage from "Effective" or "Resisted" damage differs for each enemy and damage type.''' 

If an enemy takes damage that is split between different types, each type of damage will be modified by the enemy's resistance/vulnerability to that damage, in proportion to how that damage is divided.

If damage is split between a damage type an enemy is vulnerable to, and a damage type an enemy is resistant to, both the "Resisted" and "Effective" tags will display under the enemy's damage taken.

Fell enemies are immune to Shroud damage.



Some examples:
* A Fell enemy has a multiplier of 1.2 against Blunt damage. A listed damage of 93 (100% Blunt) will display as 112 "Effective" damage.
* A Hollow enemy has a multiplier of 1.5 against Blunt damage. A listed damage of 93 (100% Blunt) will display as 140 "Effective" damage.
* A Wolf enemy has a multiplier of 1.3 against Fire damage, and 1.0 against Cutting damage. A listed damage of 62 (50% Cutting, 50% Fire) will display as 71 "Effective" damage.
* A Hollow enemy has a multiplier of 1.5 against Blunt damage, and 0.5 against Shroud damage. A listed damage of 62 (50% Blunt, 50% Shroud) will display as 62 "Effective" '''and''' "Resisted" damage. 



Tested enemy resistances are shown below. Enemies in the same "family" (Scavengers, Wildlife, Vukah, Fell) tend to have the same multipliers, but this is not always the case.

[[Valdebraise]] regorge de dangers et de mystères, habité par une grande variété d'êtres corrompus et sauvages, chacun avec sa propre histoire.

===Les déchus===
Autrefois humains et animaux de la terre, les déchus sont désormais tordus par l'influence corruptrice du Shroud, un brouillard fongique rampant qui se propage à travers Valdebraise comme une maladie vivante. Ces créatures sont déformées, leur chair consumée par des croissances fongiques, leur esprit perdu dans la folie. Certains conservent un léger écho d’eux-mêmes, rendant leur existence tragique encore plus terrifiante. Le Shroud lui-même palpite dans leurs veines, les liant à sa volonté malveillante.

===Maraudeurs===
Rendus fous par la surutilisation de l'élixir, ces maraudeurs autrefois humains parcourent désormais les terres désolées dans un état frénétique. Leurs yeux brillent d’une lumière surnaturelle et leur peau est abîmée par les brûlures chimiques causées par les substances puissantes qu’ils ingèrent. Le désespoir alimente leur violence et ils attaquent tout ce qui se trouve en vue, avides de plus d'élixir pour assouvir leur dépendance croissante. Les maraudeurs sont des créatures du chaos imprévisibles, agressives et dangereuses.

===Les Vukah===
Les insaisissables Vukah, une espèce d'êtres sensibles ressemblant à des animaux, ont commencé à dominer les régions sauvages du Valdebraise. Debout, leur corps couvert de fourrure, ils possèdent un étrange mélange de force primitive et d'intelligence rusée. Semblables en apparence à un croisement entre un Ewok et un Wookie, les Vukah utilisent une technologie primitive et des tactiques de guérilla pour protéger leurs terres. Ils peuvent paraître primitifs, mais leur vif instinct de survie et leur nature territoriale féroce en font de redoutables adversaires.

===Les creux===
Maudits et éternels, les creux sont des morts-vivants agités qui errent dans les plaines maudites et les coins sombres du Valdebraise. Leur chair pourrit, mais leurs esprits restent liés au monde des mortels par la magie noire. Vidées d'émotion et de but, ces figures tragiques recherchent les vivants, attirées par leur chaleur et leur force vitale. Méfiez-vous de leurs yeux creux, car ils ne voient aucun avenir, seulement une faim éternelle.

===Flore du Valdebraise===
La vie végétale du Valdebraise est aussi dangereuse que ses habitants, adaptés à la magie noire et à la corruption qui ravagent la terre.

===Faune du Valdebraise===
La faune du Valdebraise est un mélange de bêtes corrompues et de prédateurs naturels, dont beaucoup se sont adaptés à l'environnement hostile.

===Créatures passives===
Tous les animaux du Valdebraise ne sont pas mortels. Certaines créatures, comme les chèvres et les Hophare (grands lapins aux longues oreilles), sont des créatures paisibles, se contentant de brouter et de sautiller dans les champs.
Même au milieu du chaos, on trouve encore des animaux domestiques comme les chiens et les chats, fidèles compagnons de ceux qui ont la chance de les avoir.

== Emplacements connus ==

=== Hautes pâtures ===

* Au nord de [[Longkeep]] (Groupes jusqu'à 2 observés).
* Au long de la falaise au nord de [[Longkeep]], à l'est du [[Pont de Braelyn]] (Groupes jusqu'à 3 observés).

== Domestication ==

=== Apprivoisement ===
Les Chèvres communes peuvent être apprivoisées avec un {{item+iconright|Appât alimentaire pour chèvre}}. Elles nécessitent une caresse réussie (💛) pour être apprivoisées.

== Domestication ==

=== Apprivoisement ===
Les Chèvres frisées peuvent être apprivoisées avec de l'[[Appât alimentaire pour Chèvre]]. Elles nécessitent trois interactions de caresse réussies (💛💛💛) pour être apprivoisées.

Après avoir été amenées à votre base, elles ont besoin d'un abri, d'un [[Coussin pour animal de ferme]] et d'une [[Mangeoire pour Chèvre]] avec de la [[Nourriture pour Chèvre]]. Vous pouvez les fabriquer auprès du PNJ [[Fermier]].

=== Reproduction ===
Si on leur fournit un lit supplémentaire, un couple de Chèvres frisées a une chance de produire des petits ([[Bébé Chèvre frisée]]).

Voir [[Élevage]] pour les instructions de reproduction, la liste complète des animaux de ferme, et plus encore.

=== Production ===
Les Chèvres frisées produisent du [[Lait de Chèvre frisée]] lorsqu'elles sont abritées et nourries. Elles peuvent en stocker jusqu'à quatre (4) et n'en produiront pas davantage au-delà de cette limite tant qu'il n'aura pas été collecté.

Elles produiront également sans être nourries, mais à un rythme beaucoup plus lent. La production se poursuit quelle que soit la distance du joueur.
